title: CHAPTER 10: CURRENT AFFAIRS AND RECENT DEVELOPMENTS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Gujarat features 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, Rani ki Vav in Patan, Historic City of Ahmedabad, and Dholavira.
The Space Applications Centre (SAC) in Ahmedabad is a primary center of ISRO, crucial for developing communication and remote sensing payloads.
Infrastructure advancements in the state are highlighted by GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City) and the Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR).
Environmental and disaster management updates include response frameworks for extreme weather events such as Cyclone Biparjoy in Saurashtra and Kutch.

blocks.content: Gujarat represents a unique blend of ancient heritage and modern technological advancement, housing four UNESCO World Heritage Sites alongside state-of-the-art space and infrastructure projects.

rows: Only complete and unchanged Islamic pre-Mughal city
Subterranean stepwell built during Solanki Dynasty featured on ₹100 note
First city in India to be declared a UNESCO World Heritage City
Harappan city famous for advanced water conservation systems

items: Dholavira was inscribed as India's 40th UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021, representing the Harappan Civilization.
Rani ki Vav (Stepwell) is featured on the reverse side of the modern ₹100 banknote.
Space Applications Centre (SAC), one of the key arms of ISRO responsible for satellite payload development, is situated in Ahmedabad.
